headline: Global Briefing: Pope's Cancer, Trump Ethics Scandal, and More
summary: Pope Leo XIV was diagnosed with lung cancer and underwent successful lung surgery, according to Vatican statements. President Trump asked U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign amid ethics or corruption allegations involving a Trump donor and possible financial benefits; Guilfoyle denies the allegations. A bipartisan group of U.S. senators urged Trump to rescind a diesel deal with Russia, arguing it benefits Russia and harms Ukraine and U.S. allies. White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia's debut briefing included a verbal slip ('My president... sorry, my husband'), a claim that $54 billion of a South Korean investment package is tied to an Alaska gas project (which South Korea has expressed uncertainty about), praise for Trump, and an announcement about Guilfoyle's resignation. Palestinian officials reported that Israeli forces wounded two Palestinians in a Ramallah raid and arrested 30 Palestinians in the occupied West Bank; Israeli settlers assaulted a Palestinian family. The Iranian Navy identified an oil tanker that caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz as non-compliant with maritime rules. Apple announced a new smart home hub called HomeView, powered by Siri AI, along with an updated Apple TV 4K and a new HomePod Mini 2. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister warned that a new U.S. attack would have far-reaching consequences, while also expressing openness to diplomacy. Eight people were injured in a knife attack at a supermarket in Incheon, South Korea; the suspect was arrested. Navi Pillay was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, drawing reactions from international figures and institutions. Iranian and Egyptian foreign ministers discussed Yemen developments in a phone call. Meta launched new AI models under the name 'Muse Wonder,' claiming they are its most capable to date. Six researchers from Iran's Royan Institute were named among the world's top 2% of scientists. Formula One announced a 10-year deal for a Grand Prix in Rwanda, marking its return to Africa after 30 years. North Korea reported a test-firing of a 'tactical' ballistic missile. Trump may cut off Ukraine's access to intelligence and Starlink, according to a Politico Europe report. Iran's Foreign Minister said holding Iran's enemies accountable is an 'indisputable necessity.' Actor RJ Mitte, known for Breaking Bad, died at 34; he had cerebral palsy and was a disability rights advocate. A Delta Air Lines plane experienced a bomb threat at Ben Gurion Airport in Israel, and passengers were evacuated.
divergences: On the Pope's health, some outlets lead with the cancer diagnosis while others focus on the surgery; wording ranges from clinical to slightly emotive, and medical context varies.
In the Guilfoyle resignation, France24 emphasizes 'ethics scandal,' NPR highlights 'corruption allegations,' and The National includes her denial and donor details, which others omit.
For the Senate letter on the Russian diesel deal, The National uses a charged headline ('disastrous') and sharper quotes, while NPR is more neutral and includes the White House response.

On the White House press secretary's debut, Yonhap focuses on the $54 billion Alaska gas project claim and Seoul's uncertainty, while Indian Express highlights the verbal slip and frames the briefing as awkward.
implications: The Pope's cancer diagnosis raises concerns about his health and leadership of the Catholic Church. The Guilfoyle resignation request signals ongoing ethics scrutiny in the Trump administration and could affect U.S.-Greece relations. The bipartisan Senate letter on the Russian diesel deal indicates congressional pressure on Trump's Russia policy, with potential implications for Ukraine and U.S. allies. The White House press secretary's debut, with its slip and policy claims, may shape media relations and public perception of the administration's competence. Israeli-Palestinian tensions remain high after the Ramallah raid and settler violence. The Strait of Hormuz tanker fire could affect maritime security and oil shipping. Apple's new products intensify competition in the smart home market. Iran's warnings and diplomatic outreach suggest ongoing regional tensions. The South Korea knife attack renews focus on public safety and repeat offenders. Navi Pillay's Nobel Peace Prize highlights international justice issues and may strain Israel-U.S. relations. Meta's new AI models could shift the competitive landscape in AI. Formula One's return to Africa could boost Rwanda's economy but raises human rights questions. North Korea's missile test continues to challenge regional security. Potential U.S. cutoff of intelligence and Starlink to Ukraine could weaken Ukraine's defense. Iran's accountability stance may escalate tensions. RJ Mitte's death brings attention to cerebral palsy and disability advocacy. The Delta bomb threat underscores ongoing security concerns at airports.
